nm ROIC CHECK prefetch roic_last 0.1397 is FY2024 (FY2025 invested capital missing in the screen, roic null for FY2025). FY2025 NOPAT 1,410 is on 1,824 operating income. Invested capital check at FY2025: equity 12,964 + debt (long-term debt not in pf for FY2025; FY2024 1,489) less cash 3,726 and short-term investments 2,558 gives roughly 8.6-9.3bn before leases; goodwill rose to 3,578 (Moveworks, Armis acquisitions in 2026 will add more invested capital: Armis closed in 2026 per 10-Q), so ROIC on FY2025 about 15-16% before acquisitions and will fall in FY2026. Restricted cash, operating leases not adjusted.

Q3 2026 GAAP EPS 0.27 vs 0.48 a year ago: the GAAP earnings base is falling (acquisition amortization, SBC +29%), so GAAP P/E is flattering neither past nor present; not a peak-earnings case.

nm CONSENSUS only a pre-Q3 snapshot was found (attributed, non-independent aggregator, basis not stated): FY2026 EPS 4.12 (51 analysts, 2026-10-17); Q3 2026 consensus before the report: EPS 1.04 and revenue 4,135 (Chartmill preview, a note not a row) versus reported total revenue 4,106 (-0.7%) and GAAP EPS 0.27, so the aggregator's revenue consensus was above the reported figure while the company beat its own subscription guidance (3,988 vs guided 3,975-3,980). Other secondhand figures disagree on basis: FY2026 revenue 16.0-16.2bn, FY2027 revenue about 19bn, FY2027 EPS between 3.0 and 5.0 (GAAP vs non-GAAP unresolved): not registered as rows. No post-2026-10-28 consensus found. Targets, if any, are opinions: none used.

nm TRACK RECORD subscription revenue vs guided midpoint, 6 periods (Q1 2025 to Q3 2026, Q4 2024 and Q2 2026 guides not in the saved releases): ratios 1.0025, 1.0266, 1.0112, 1.0120, 1.0051, 1.0026, mean about 1.010, 6 beats, 0 misses: conservative guider, beats the midpoint by about 0.3% to 2.7%, bigger beats in 2025 Q2 when FX and the April guide were cautious. Q3 2026 beat the high end (3,988 vs 3,975-3,980) but was only +0.26% over the midpoint, the smallest beat except Q1 2025 and Q3 2026: the cushion is thinning while the stock fell sharply.
